vendors.tagline: Native graph database with GraphRAG libraries, Aura Agent, and MCP servers.
vendors.verdictNote: Neo4j gives a graph model, Cypher, vector search, and agents, but no governed metric or dimension objects over warehouse tables.

artifacts.format: JDBC driver with SQL2Cypher; listed as coming soon to Labs

metrics.n: No metric object type. Aggregates are written as Cypher; Aura Agent Cypher templates can pin a parameterized query.

dimensions.n: No dimension or time-grain objects. Teams model categories as node labels or properties.

relationships.n: Relationships are first-class typed edges with properties. Virtual Graph maps foreign keys to relationships (Preview).

synonyms.n: Aura Agent holds agent instructions and tool descriptions that the LLM reads. No synonym object type.

verifiedQueries.n: Aura Agent Cypher templates are predefined, parameterized queries the agent calls as tools. They are not question-query pairs.

nl2sql.n: Aura Agent Text2Cypher tool (GA Feb 2026) writes Cypher, not SQL. Neo4j's EAP guide calls it a fallback to templates.

ontology.n: Business ontology is in Neo4j Context Engine, private preview (Oct 2026). Graph schema works as an ontology by convention.

graph.n: Cypher property graph queries plus Graph Data Science algorithms. Cypher over Snowflake tables via Virtual Graph (Preview).

vector.n: Vector indexes and similarity search; the neo4j-graphrag library and Aura Agent both use them.

mcp.n: Official Neo4j MCP server (GA announced Dec 2025) and Aura Agent hosted MCP endpoints with OAuth.

governance.n: Virtual Graph runs queries under a read-only Snowflake user, so source RBAC applies (Preview). Context Engine adds governance (private preview).

openStandard.n: No OSI listing found. Labs MCP servers are MIT licensed. Aura Agent exposes standard MCP and REST endpoints.

offers: Aura Agent builds an agent from the graph schema, with Cypher template, similarity search, and Text2Cypher tools (GA Feb 2026).
Hosted MCP and REST endpoints for agents; MCP is read-only. Public agents bill per agent-hour from March 2026.
Official MCP server tools: get-schema, read-cypher, write-cypher, list-gds-procedures. Read-only mode available; latest release v1.6.1 (Oct 2026).
neo4j-graphrag Python library: vector retrieval, Text2CypherRetriever, and a knowledge graph builder pipeline (some parts experimental).
Warehouse links: Graph Analytics for Snowflake (Marketplace), Spark connector for Databricks, Dataflow templates for BigQuery, Aura Data Importer.
Virtual Graph (Preview, Jun 2026) translates Cypher to Snowflake SQL in place, with no copy; the translation is rule-based.
gaps: No metric, dimension, or time-grain objects, so governed KPIs stay in a warehouse semantic layer.
Text2Cypher writes Cypher, not SQL. Warehouse data must be loaded, mapped through Virtual Graph (Preview), or queried separately.
The Virtual Graph article covers Snowflake only. The Unity Catalog connector for Databricks is listed as coming soon to Labs.
MCP read-only mode relies on EXPLAIN query classification. The README warns misclassified custom procedures may bypass it.
Business ontology (Context Engine) is private preview. Neo4j is not named in OSI partner lists.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Keep NL-to-SQL on the warehouse semantic layer. Use Neo4j for multi-hop and relationship questions, with Cypher templates first and Text2Cypher as fallback. To reach warehouse data, import with Aura Data Importer or the Spark connector, or try Virtual Graph (Preview) for Snowflake.

metrics.n: No metric object found in docs. A Big Spender segment is encoded once in the ontology (AWS post).

dimensions.n: No dimension or time-grain objects found in docs. Class hierarchies in the ontology are the closest equivalent.

relationships.n: Ontology properties plus mappings define relationships. Shared IRIs let virtual graphs join Aurora and Redshift without ETL (AWS post).

verifiedQueries.n: Voicebox uses few-shot examples alongside the ontology as domain context.

nl2sql.n: Voicebox writes SPARQL; Stardog compiles it into a multi-SQL query plan from mappings. SPARQL is the intermediate language.

ontology.n: Ontologies and reasoning are the core product. Pre-configured Knowledge Kits ship with Voicebox.

graph.n: SPARQL over RDF knowledge graphs. Virtual graphs rewrite SPARQL into each source's native query language.

vector.n: Built-in vector store for concept matching and for RAG over PDF and DOCX files indexed by a Spark pipeline.

mcp.n: Official stardog-cloud-mcp exposes Voicebox tools. Local mode stable, remote mode beta; needs a Voicebox API token.

governance.n: Named-graph security by role, lineage per answer, and exportable audit logs of questions and generated SPARQL.

openStandard.n: RDF, SPARQL, and R2RML supported; SMS2 is Stardog-specific. Stardog is not named in OSI partner lists.

offers: Virtual graphs query SQL sources in place by rewriting SPARQL to native SQL; optional materialization with virtual import.
Mapping sources include Snowflake, Databricks SQL, BigQuery, Redshift, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, and Synapse.
Voicebox: natural language to SPARQL to SQL, with few-shot examples, lineage, answer provenance, and CSV audit reports.
Stardog Cloud MCP server exposes voicebox_ask, voicebox_generate_query, and voicebox_settings to agents.
AWS reference design (Jul 2026) uses Bedrock AgentCore and shared IRIs to join Aurora and Redshift without ETL.
gaps: No first-party metric or measure object found; metrics must be modeled in the ontology or SPARQL.
The NL path runs through SPARQL, so SQL teams learn mappings (SMS2, R2RML) and ontology modeling.
Docs state External LLM agent answers may contain hallucinations; the product page says hallucination-managed.
MCP needs a Voicebox API token limited to certain accounts; multi-agent orchestration is private preview.
Stardog does not appear in OSI partner lists, and SMS2 mappings are not portable to other tools.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Model the ontology, map warehouse tables with virtual graphs, and ask through Voicebox, which writes SPARQL that Stardog turns into SQL. Agents can reach Voicebox through the Stardog Cloud MCP server, or call SPARQL directly (AWS Bedrock AgentCore reference, Jul 2026). Keep governed metrics in a warehouse semantic layer.

vendors.nl2sqlPath: For NL-to-SQL on Snowflake, use Snowflake semantic views and Cortex Analyst for metrics. Add RelationalAI when questions need rules, graph analysis, or optimization that SQL does not express; reasoner outputs return as tables that Snowflake Intelligence and agents can read.

snippet.title: PyRel (Python): concept, property, subtype rule, query (comments trimmed)
snippet.code:
from relationalai.semantics import Integer, Model, String

m = Model("PeopleModel")
Person = m.Concept("Person")
Person.name = m.Property(f"{Person} is named {String:name}")
Person.age = m.Property(f"{Person} is {Integer:age} years old")
m.define(Person.new(name="Alice", age=10), Person.new(name="Bob", age=30))

# Adult is a subtype of Person, defined by a rule
Adult = m.Concept("Adult", extends=[Person])
m.define(Adult(Person)).where(Person.age >= 18)

q = m.select(Adult.name, Adult.age)
q.inspect()

notes.text: A business-facing layer over physical data that names tables and columns as business terms; Business Objects filed a patent for the idea in 1991. In 2026 vendors use it for governed metrics, dimensions, and joins (dbt Semantic Layer, Snowflake semantic views), or, at Stardog, for an ontology of concepts, rules, and constraints. It is the broad umbrella; metrics layer, semantic model, and ontology are narrower or alternative parts of it.

sources.t: Stardog: Why every AI system needs a semantic layer

notes.text: A central definition of how each metric is calculated, placed between the warehouse and BI tools, that returns SQL for a metric request (Benn Stancil, April 2021). It covers measures and the dimensions to slice them, not entities, rules, or glossary terms, so it is narrower than a semantic layer. Today it ships inside products such as dbt MetricFlow and Databricks metric views; I found no primary source that defines the label 'metrics store'.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Semantic layer (lists metrics layer and headless BI as names)

notes.text: A formal, explicit specification of a shared conceptualization of a domain: classes, properties, relations, and constraints (Gruber, 1993). W3C describes OWL 2 ontologies as formalized vocabularies of terms. It is the schema level, while a knowledge graph is the data that uses it; RelationalAI says ontologies add entity identity, relationships with multiplicity, and constraints beyond the dimensional semantics of metrics.

A graph of data meant to accumulate and convey knowledge of the real world, with nodes for entities and edges for relations (Hogan et al., ACM Computing Surveys 2021); Google popularized the term in 2012 as 'things, not strings'. Neo4j adds that a knowledge graph is a graph plus meaning and organizing principles such as taxonomies or ontologies. It models entities and facts rather than metric definitions, and it holds instance data where an ontology holds the schema.

notes.text: Current usage comes from the Foundation Capital essay 'AI's trillion-dollar opportunity: Context graphs' by Jaya Gupta and Ashu Garg. It defines a context graph as 'a living record of decision traces stitched across entities and time so precedent becomes searchable', not the model's chain-of-thought, and never mentions knowledge graphs or ontologies. Exact original date is unverified: the page metadata shows Oct 23, 2026, and the essay cites a post whose URL carries 121225, so it was written after mid-December 2025.

notes.text: Vendors use the term in different ways. Atlan and Neo4j follow the decision-trace idea (Atlan: 'a specialized knowledge graph that captures decision traces'; Neo4j: a knowledge graph plus the agent's conversations, tool calls, decisions, and outcomes), while Google's Knowledge Catalog (renamed from Dataplex Universal Catalog on 10 Apr 2026) calls its metadata metamodel an 'active context graph'. RelationalAI and Stardog prefer 'context layer'.

notes.text: An inventory of an organization's data assets with metadata that helps people find, understand, manage, and access data (IBM). It is a discovery and governance tool: it holds descriptions, lineage, and glossary links, but it does not define queryable metrics like a semantic layer. Catalogs now add AI context; Google renamed Dataplex Universal Catalog to Knowledge Catalog in April 2026, and data.world builds its catalog on a knowledge graph.

notes.text: A governed vocabulary of business terms, grouped in categories, with owners and relations such as synonym and related term, that can link to data assets and columns (Google Knowledge Catalog docs). It records meaning, not query logic, so it differs from a semantic layer. It is also business-facing, where a data dictionary describes dataset fields, types, and allowed values (IBM).

notes.text: The artifact that stores a semantic layer's definitions, and the word has no single meaning. A Power BI semantic model is an Analysis Services tabular model with data preparation queries, relationships, and calculations; Snowflake used 'semantic model' for stage-based YAML files, now called legacy and replaced by schema-level semantic views. Stardog uses 'semantic models (ontologies)'.

notes.text: Retrieval-augmented generation that connects facts in a graph instead of scattering them across isolated text chunks, so answers can follow relationships. Neo4j's agentic variant lets an AI agent choose between vector search, graph traversal, and schema inspection at each step.

A vendor-neutral JSON and YAML spec for semantic layer constructs (datasets, metrics, dimensions, relationships, context), launched by Snowflake and partners on 23 Sep 2025; v0.1 went live under Apache 2.0 on 27 Jan 2026. It entered the Apache Incubator on 22 Jun 2026 and the rename to Apache Ossie (incubating) was announced on 8 to 10 Jul 2026. RelationalAI is a launch partner; Stardog, Neo4j, and data.world do not appear on the partner lists I read.

ServiceNow signed a definitive agreement to buy data.world in May 2025 (reported 7 May at Knowledge 2025), and its quarterly filing says it completed the acquisition in July 2025. The exact closing day and price are not disclosed; ServiceNow calls the deal not material. data.world's site says 'data.world is now part of ServiceNow!' and that data.world Enterprise continues unchanged.
